newsitem.title: FRANCE: Camdessus sees early decision on debt relief.
newsitem.headline: Camdessus sees early decision on debt relief.

text.p: Uganda, Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso and Bolivia should be among the first to benefit from a new initiative to lift the debt burden from poor nations, IMF head Michel Camdessus said on Tuesday.

He said he expected a decision in the next few weeks on providing enhanced debt relief under a joint initiative agreed last year by the International Monetary Fund, World Bank and Paris Club of creditor nations.

"I think that in the next few weeks we will be able to make a decision on a first group of countries, among whom there is Uganda, Burkina Faso, Bolivia and Ivory Coast," he told reporters after meeting French President Jacques Chirac.
Uganda, has long been cited as a likely first candidate for debt relief, though France has pressed hard to ensure its own former colonies benefit from the initiative.
Uganda, a former British colony, has irked France through its alleged role in backing rebels fighting in Zaire, whose President Mobuto Sese Seko has been supported by Paris.

French officials deny suggestions this might affect its view on the debt initiative, but have stressed they want as many countries as possible to benefit, and President Jacques Chirac has often pledged to help France's former colonies in Africa.

Paris had promised in particular to support Ivory Coast, a key ally in west Africa. As a somewhat richer country it may not technically fully qualify for debt relief under criteria still being discussed at the IMF.

Camdessus said that while the cost to Ivory Coast of debt service charges was very heavy as a proportion of budget revenues, it was slightly less so as a proportion of export revenues -- one of the criteria to qualify for debt relief.

"It is a question which will be discussed at the board of the IMF and World Bank. I have made proposals which should produce a positive result for Ivory Coast, but points of view are still a little divergent," he said.

One argument likely to be put forward is that Ivory Coast should not be punished for having stronger export revenues, since this reflected efforts to open up its economy, one international financial source said.
The debt initiative is due to be discussed at the twice-yearly meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Washington later this month.
The aim is to help countries implementing economic reforms, but for whom the benefits of economic growth are wiped out by heavy debt service charges.
The Paris Club of creditor nations has agreed it could write off up to 80 percent of the debt due during the time a country implements IMF-backed economic reforms.
Currently the best terms of debt relief available, so-called Naples terms, allow for a write-off of two-thirds of the debt.
The IMF and World Bank, which became themselves big lenders to poor countries as they tried to help them out, will also act to reduce debt owed to them.

The initiative was agreed in principle at a summit of the Group of Seven rich nations in Lyon, France, last year, which Chirac had pledged to use to tackle the plight of poor nations, marginalised by economic development in the rich world.
